deQR decode fixtures

Load the unpacked extension, then open this page. A Reveal badge must appear on every image in the first three sections and on none of the images in "Should not be badged". Images are 168px on screen; the originals are larger.

Formats - all four must decode

PNG, JPG and WEBP are decoded from canvas pixels. Remote SVG and inline SVG go through the serialize-to-data-URL path, which is the only format with distinct handling. If the JPG and WEBP tiles show as broken images, those fixtures were not generated: they need sips and cwebp, unlike PNG and SVG. Run pnpm fixtures.

Risk levels - check the panel, not just the badge

Sizes

Reachability - both must be badged

Two ways a real page hides a QR from a naive scanner. The overlaid one is what a loading spinner or a lightbox trigger does: the image never sees the pointer, so hover has to be a hit test against the rect instead of a mouseenter listener. The shadow one is invisible to any selector run on the document, so open roots have to be walked separately.

Should not be badged

A badge on any of these is a false positive: it means the prefilter is too loose and the decoder is being paid for nothing.

Cross-origin, no CORS

This image is served from another origin without CORS headers, so the canvas is tainted and deQR cannot read a single pixel. Expect the amber Allow deQR badge. Clicking it opens the options page; grant that origin, reload, and the badge must become Reveal. This is the one flow that has to be walked by hand.
